properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 18 at 8:07AM CDT until October 21 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a Flood Advisory
for the following rivers in Texas...

Beaver Creek near Electra affecting Wichita and Wilbarger Counties.

For the Beaver Creek (NW TX)...including Electra...elevated river
levels are forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 815 PM CDT.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Beaver Creek near Electra.

* WHEN...From this morning to Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, Shallow and short duration flooding of
lowlands along and near the creek may occur in southern Wilbarger
County and southwestern Wichita County.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 AM CDT Sunday the stage was 12.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 24.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 23.0 feet
Tuesday morning.
- Action stage is 22.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 24.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM THIS MORNING TO WEDNESDAY MORNING

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 15 at 8:39AM CDT until October 19 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...
Oklahoma...

Red River near Burkburnett affecting Wichita, Cotton, Tillman,
Jefferson and Clay Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Red River near Burkburnett.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Near bankfull conditions extend along the
Red River near Davidson... Oklahoma downstream to areas near
Burkburnett and Taylor... Oklahoma.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.7 feet
Saturday evening.
- Action stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
